newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler trying to keep Mercedes chief - sources.
newsitem.headline: Daimler trying to keep Mercedes chief - sources.

text.p: Germany's biggest industrial group Daimler-Benz AG was trying Monday to persuade Mercedes-Benz chief Helmut Werner to stay on following reports he had threatened to resign, industry sources said.

Following a highly publicised dispute over a planned company reorganization, Daimler management board Chairman Juergen Schrempp had even offered Werner the post of chairman of a restructured Daimler group, the sources said.
Werner has opposed a plan by Schrempp to more closely integrate the profitable Mercedes car and truck operation that has become a cash cow for Daimler.

Werner's contract as management board member of Daimler, which expires at the end of 1997, is up for renewal at a supervisory board meeting on Nov. 6. His contract as head of Mercedes runs until 1999.
But given a possible management revamp, the board may delay a decision to extend the contract, industry sources said, adding that this could prompt Werner to resign.
"Everybody wants to keep Werner in the company," one source said.
The deputy chairman of the supervisory board, Karl Feuerstein said in an interview that any supervisory board decision on a restructuring of Daimler would probably not be taken at the Nov. 6 meeting.

"Maybe the decision won't be taken this year," said Feuerstein. Feuerstein said he was not opposed to the idea of a new structure but believed Daimler's automotive business must remain a single entity.
"We will measure all proposals according to this demand," he said.

The four-member executive committee of the supervisory board, consisting of two employee and two shareholder representatives, will discuss the plans for a management restructuring at a meeting on Tuesday, Feuerstein said.
